events.title: IBM Simon Personal Communicator released
events.summary: BellSouth began selling the [IBM] Simon in August 1994 — a touchscreen phone with email, calendar, and third-party apps years before the [iPhone].
events.about: The Simon combined a cellular phone with a [PDA] — users tapped a stylus on a monochrome LCD for fax, email, and address book apps. It was bulky and expensive, but proved the smartphone concept before Palm and BlackBerry refined mobile messaging. Mobile developers today trace a lineage through these early converged devices.

narrative.whyChosen: The [IBM] Simon was the first phone sold with [PDA] features and downloadable applications.
narrative.whyImportant: It demonstrated demand for pocket computers that also made calls — a decade before smartphones went mainstream.
narrative.problemSolved: Business travelers carried separate phones and organizers; convergence needed a single touchscreen device.
